rules.title: Boston ban on source-of-income (rental assistance) discrimination in renting
rules.requirement: In Boston, a landlord may not refuse to rent to you or treat you differently because you pay with rental assistance, such as a Section 8, social security disability, or veterans voucher. If this happens, you can file a complaint with the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
rules.key_value: Rental assistance (e.g., Section 8 vouchers) is a protected class
rules.coverage_conditions: All housing rentals in the City of Boston; enforced by the Boston Fair Housing Commission.
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations (Boston Fair Housing Commission); specific code section not stated in document
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance.
rules.penalty: The Commission investigates complaints and tries to resolve them; specific penalties not stated.

notes: The document is a general Boston.gov page about fair housing. It lists protected classes, including 'Rental Assistance', which the page explains with the example of renters using Section 8 vouchers. The page gives no municipal code section, no effective date and no exemptions, so I left the citation descriptive. I believe the ordinance is the Boston Fair Housing ordinance in Boston Municipal Code Chapter 10, but I didn't use that because the document doesn't say so. The page also says the Commission enforces state and federal law, but it doesn't describe any specific state rule, so I didn't extract a Massachusetts state rule. The page doesn't mention criminal history or any other in-scope categories. The other protected classes (race, sex and so on) are general anti-discrimination rules, which are outside the six categories.
